verdict_reason: Repaired and verified. The disk-offloaded collector returned ONE tensor for the whole corpus while consistency.py treats each list element as one document, so every within-document control silently became a corpus-wide derangement -- a storage-induced change to the declared statistic. After retaining per-document lengths and returning per-document views of the memmaps, the two storage routes agree exactly: on a 4-document gpt2 run all 9 numeric outputs are identical between BLME_DISK_OFFLOAD=0 and =1, the concatenated logits/labels/hidden tensors are bit-identical, and the document lengths match ([9,7,10] on a 3-document control). The bytes were never in question; only the segmentation was.
comparable_reason: No comparability defect established on the axes measured.
github_reason: No released reference for this composite statistic; verified by ROUTE EQUIVALENCE, which is the property the defect broke. tests/tasks/test_prediction_alignment_storage.py.
confounds_reason: Route equivalence is now pinned by a regression test that asserts identical per-document lengths and bit-identical concatenated tensors, so a future storage change cannot silently redefine the statistic again.
